practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 85(1) of the Constitution empowers the President to summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit. The maximum gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum permissible time gap between two consecutive sessions of Parliament under the Indian Constitution?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 85, the President shall summon each House of Parliament from time to time so that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. Thus, Parliament must meet at least twice a year.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following terms refers to the termination of a session of Parliament by an order of the President?
practiceQuestions.sol: Prorogation means the termination of a session of Parliament by an order of the President. It differs from adjournment, which only terminates a sitting and not a session, and is ordered by the presiding officer of the House.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the power to adjourn a sitting of the Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: An adjournment suspends the work in a sitting for a specified time, which may be hours, days, or weeks. The power of adjournment lies with the presiding officer of the House (Speaker in Lok Sabha and Chairman in Rajya Sabha).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the term used when a sitting of Parliament is terminated without naming a day for reassembly (indefinitely)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Adjournment sine die means terminating a sitting of Parliament for an indefinite period. When the House is adjourned without naming a day for reassembly, it is called adjournment sine die. It is done by the presiding officer.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following sessions of the Indian Parliament is traditionally the longest session?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Budget Session, which extends from February to May, is traditionally the longest session of the Indian Parliament because it deals with the presentation and discussion of the Union Budget and related financial bills.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the three annual sessions of the Indian Parliament is usually the shortest?
opts: All sessions are of equal duration
practiceQuestions.sol: The Winter Session, held generally from mid-November to mid-December, is usually the shortest of the three regular parliamentary sessions in India.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum quorum required to transact business in either House of Parliament?
opts: One-third of the total members of the House
One-tenth of the total members of the House
One-fourth of the total members of the House
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 100(3) of the Constitution, the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of members of that House.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies recommends the dates and duration of parliamentary sessions in India?
opts: Speaker of the Lok Sabha in consultation with the Prime Minister
practiceQuestions.sol: In India, the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs (CCPA) takes decisions regarding the dates and duration of parliamentary sessions. Based on its recommendations, the President summons the Houses.

practiceQuestions.q: The first hour of every parliamentary sitting is traditionally allotted for which of the following?
practiceQuestions.sol: The first hour of every parliamentary sitting is designated for Question Hour, during which members ask questions and ministers usually give answers.

practiceQuestions.q: How does prorogation of the House affect pending bills and other business in the Indian Parliament?
opts: It lapses all bills pending in both Houses of Parliament.
It does not affect the bills or any other business pending in Parliament.
It lapses only the bills pending in the Lok Sabha.
It dissolves the Lok Sabha automatically.
practiceQuestions.sol: Prorogation terminates a session, but it does not affect the bills or any other business pending in either House of Parliament. However, all pending notices (other than for bills) lapse upon prorogation. Dissolution, on the other hand, causes certain bills to lapse.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the unique feature of 'Zero Hour' in the Indian parliamentary system compared to other parliamentary democracies?
opts: It is explicitly mentioned in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha.
It is an Indian innovation in the parliamentary procedure not explicitly mentioned in the rule book.
It is a mandatory constitutional provision under Article 118.
It is reserved exclusively for the Prime Minister's address.
practiceQuestions.sol: Zero Hour is an Indian innovation in parliamentary procedures existing since 1962. It is an informal device available to members of Parliament to raise matters without prior notice, and it is not mentioned in the rule book.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the classification of parliamentary sessions not strictly mandated by the Constitution of India in terms of specific names?
opts: The Constitution only prescribes the frequency and maximum gap between sessions, leaving nomenclature to parliamentary convention.
Parliamentary sessions can only be called upon the direct order of the Supreme Court.
The British Parliament dictates the names of sessions in India.
The Constitution prohibits the President from naming sessions.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indian Constitution under Article 85 mandates that six months shall not intervene between two sessions, ensuring at least two sessions a year. However, terms like Budget, Monsoon, and Winter sessions are established by convention, not explicitly defined in the text of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens to a Bill passed by both Houses of Parliament when the President returns it for reconsideration and the session is subsequently prorogued?
opts: The Bill lapses due to prorogation.
Prorogation does not cause a Bill returned by the President for reconsideration to lapse.
The Bill is automatically treated as rejected.
A fresh election must be called for the Parliament to consider it.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 111, when the President returns a bill for reconsideration, the Houses must reconsider it. Prorogation does not affect pending or returned bills because a bill that has been passed by both Houses and is awaiting assent or is returned for reconsideration does not lapse on prorogation.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of parliamentary sittings, what is the significance of the 'Casting Vote'?
opts: It is the vote cast by the President during a deadlock.
It is exercised by the presiding officer only to resolve a tie and cannot be used in the first instance.
It is the vote cast by the Prime Minister to pass money bills.
It is an extra vote given to every Member of Parliament during budget sessions.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 100(1), all questions at any sitting of either House shall be determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, other than the Chairman or Speaker or person acting as such. The presiding officer does not vote in the first instance, but exercises a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does a dissolution of the Lok Sabha affect pending bills differently than prorogation?
opts: Dissolution ends the very life of the Lok Sabha, causing certain pending bills to lapse, whereas prorogation only ends a session without terminating the House's life.
Dissolution has no impact on any bill, while prorogation lapses all bills.
Dissolution is ordered by the Prime Minister, while prorogation is ordered by the Supreme Court.
There is no functional difference between dissolution and prorogation.
practiceQuestions.sol: Dissolution destroys the representative character of the Lok Sabha completely. As per Article 107, bills pending in the Lok Sabha (whether originating there or transmitted from Rajya Sabha) lapse on dissolution. Prorogation, however, leaves the House intact and does not cause bills to lapse.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the correct procedural mechanism when a House of Parliament is adjourned sine die?
opts: The President issues a formal notification to dissolve the House.
The presiding officer suspends business without setting a date for resumption, which is usually followed shortly by a presidential order of prorogation.
Members automatically lose their membership and fresh elections are triggered.
The Supreme Court takes over the legislative functions temporarily.
practiceQuestions.sol: When the work of a session is completed, the House is adjourned sine die by the presiding officer. Within a few days, the President issues a notification for the prorogation of the session. Thus, adjournment sine die precedes prorogation.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are Question Hour and Zero Hour critical for ensuring executive accountability during parliamentary sessions?
opts: They allow members to directly question ministers regarding government policies, omissions, and administrative actions.
They give absolute legislative power to individual backbenchers over the Cabinet.
They are used exclusively to pass constitutional amendment bills without debate.
They provide a mechanism for the judiciary to issue directives to Parliament.
practiceQuestions.sol: Question Hour and Zero Hour are core instruments of parliamentary oversight. They compel ministers to account for their ministries' administration and policies on the floor of the House, thereby maintaining the principle of ministerial responsibility to the legislature.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional implication if the Lok Sabha passes a motion of no-confidence during a parliamentary session?
opts: Only the Prime Minister must resign, while the rest of the Cabinet remains in office.
The entire Council of Ministers must resign collectively as they lose majority support.
The session is immediately extended by one month.
The President takes direct control of financial matters.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 75(3) of the Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. If a no-confidence motion is passed, the entire government falls and the Council of Ministers must resign collectively.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the practice of 'Guillotine' operate during the financial business of the Budget Session in Parliament?
opts: It is a rule where all members who disrupt the session are permanently expelled.
It is a special procedure where pending demands for grants are put to vote together without discussion due to lack of time.
It is an absolute veto power held by the Rajya Sabha over Lok Sabha's financial bills.
It is the formal method used by the President to prorogue Parliament abruptly.
practiceQuestions.sol: During the Budget Session, Parliament discusses demands for grants. Due to time constraints, discussion cannot be completed for all ministries. On the last allotted day, the Speaker puts all remaining outstanding demands to vote together without discussion—a process known as 'Guillotine'.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the summoning of Parliament:
1. The power to summon each House of Parliament is vested in the Prime Minister of India.
2. The Constitution mandates that there should not be a gap of more than six months between two consecutive sessions of Parliament.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the power to summon each House of Parliament is vested in the President, not the Prime Minister (though the President acts on the aid and advice of the Cabinet headed by the PM). Statement 2 is correct as Article 85 stipulates a maximum gap of six months between sessions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Adjournment and Prorogation:
1. Adjournment terminates both a sitting and a session of Parliament.
2. Prorogation is ordered by the President of India.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because adjournment only terminates a sitting of Parliament, not a session. Prorogation terminates a session. Statement 2 is correct as prorogation is done by the President under Article 85(2)(a).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the impact of Dissolution on pending bills:
1. A bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha, regardless of where it originated.
2. A bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha does not lapse upon dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: As per Article 107, any bill pending in the Lok Sabha (originating in Lok Sabha or transmitted from Rajya Sabha) lapses on dissolution. Statement 2 is incorrect because a bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha *does* lapse on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Quorum of Parliament:
1. The quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is fixed at one-fifth of the total members of that House.
2. If there is no quorum during a meeting, it is the duty of the presiding officer either to adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the quorum is one-tenth (1/10th), not one-fifth, of the total members of the House under Article 100(3). Statement 2 is correct: under Article 100(4), if there is no quorum, the presiding officer must either suspend the meeting or adjourn the House.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the three regular sessions of the Indian Parliament:
1. The Budget Session is the longest of all three sessions and runs from February to May.
2. The Winter Session is traditionally the second session of the calendar year.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Budget Session is the longest session, held from February to May. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Winter Session is the third session of the year (held from Nov-Dec), while the Monsoon Session is the second session (held from July-Sep).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Question Hour:
1. It is the first hour of a parliamentary sitting.
2. Starred questions require a written answer and no supplementary questions can be asked thereon.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct as Question Hour occupies the first hour of every sitting. Statement 2 is incorrect because *starred* questions require an *oral* answer, allowing supplementary questions to be asked. Unstarred questions require written answers.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding bills that do NOT lapse on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha:
1. A bill pending in the Rajya Sabha which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha lapses upon dissolution.
2. A bill pending for assent of the President does not lapse upon dissolution.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because a bill pending in the Rajya Sabha which has *not* been passed by the Lok Sabha does *not* lapse on dissolution. Statement 2 is correct: a bill pending for the President's assent (or returned by him for reconsideration) does not lapse.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the Presiding Officer during a session:
1. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha can adjourn the House sine die.
2. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha has the power to prorogue the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The presiding officer (Speaker in Lok Sabha, Chairman in Rajya Sabha) can adjourn the House or adjourn it sine die. Statement 2 is incorrect because prorogation is an executive power exercised exclusively by the President, not by the presiding officer.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Joint Sitting of Parliament:
1. A joint sitting can be summoned by the President to resolve a deadlock over any type of bill, including Constitutional Amendment Bills and Money Bills.
2. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because a joint sitting cannot be summoned for Money Bills (as Rajya Sabha has no veto over them) or Constitutional Amendment Bills (which must be passed by each House separately under Article 368). Statement 2 is correct: the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over joint sittings.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Lame-duck' session:
1. It refers to the last session of the existing Lok Sabha after a new Lok Sabha has been elected.
2. Members of Parliament who could not get re-elected to the new Lok Sabha are called lame-ducks.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. A lame-duck session refers to the last session of the existing Lok Sabha after a new Lok Sabha has been elected. Members of the existing Lok Sabha who failed to get re-elected to the new house are known as 'lame-ducks'.
